title: Maximize Subarray Sum After Removing All Occurrences of One Element
statement:
`nums` is an array of integers. At most once, you may pick an integer `x` and delete all of its occurrences from `nums`, but only if at least one element is left afterwards.

Return the greatest sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray over every array you can end up with, including `nums` itself when you delete nothing.
notes:
## Intuition

Rebuilding the array for every distinct value and scanning each copy costs O(n²) when most values are distinct. Yet removing `x` changes only the positions where `x` sits.

A segment tree exploits that. Each node summarises its range by its total, best subarray, best prefix and best suffix; two neighbouring ranges combine in O(1), and the root answers for the whole array. Blanking the positions of `x`, reading the root and restoring them costs O(log n) per position.

## Approach

1. A leaf holds one value in all four fields. `EMPTY` (total 0, the rest `-Infinity`) marks a removed or padding position and leaves any merge unchanged.
2. `merge`: the best subarray lies in the left part, in the right part, or crosses the middle as `left.suffix + right.prefix`; a prefix may run through the whole left part, a suffix through the whole right part.
3. Build the tree bottom-up over `size` leaves, a power of two, padded with `EMPTY`.
4. List each value's indices in `positions`; start `answer` at the root's `best` (no removal).
5. For each value, set its leaves to `EMPTY`, compare `tree[1].best` with `answer`, and put the leaves back. Return `answer`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [-3, 2, -2, -1, 3, -2, 3]`. The root starts with `best = 4` (`3 - 2 + 3`). In first-seen order: removing `-3` or `2` keeps 4; removing `-2` blanks indices 2 and 5, the root sees `[-3, 2, -1, 3, 3]` and its best becomes `2 - 1 + 3 + 3 = 7`; removing `-1` gives 4 and removing `3` gives 2. The answer is 7.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n): each index is blanked and restored once, each change walking from leaf to root.
- Space: O(n) for the tree and the position lists.

## Pitfalls

- Blanking with 0 is wrong: a stretch of zeros would count as a subarray with sum 0 even when everything left is negative.
- Subarrays are non-empty, so an empty range has `best`, `prefix` and `suffix` of `-Infinity`.
- Removing the only distinct value is not allowed; its root `best` is `-Infinity`, so it never wins.
- Restore the leaves after each value, or later removals still see earlier ones missing.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `EMPTY` | node for a removed or padding position |
| `leaf`, `merge` | make a leaf; combine two neighbouring ranges |
| `size` | number of leaves, a power of two at least `nums.length` |
| `tree` | the nodes; `node` has children `2 * node` and `2 * node + 1`, and `tree[1]` covers all |
| `update` | puts `item` in the leaf for `index` and recombines its ancestors |
| `positions` | each value mapped to its indices |
| `value`, `indices` | the value being removed and its positions |
| `answer` | best subarray sum found so far |

narration.2: An empty range has total 0 and no subarray at all, so merging with EMPTY changes nothing.
narration.3: A single value is its own total, best subarray, best prefix and best suffix.
narration.6: The best subarray lies inside one part or crosses the middle as the left's suffix plus the right's prefix.
narration.7: The best prefix stays in the left part or runs through all of it into the right's prefix.
narration.8: The best suffix stays in the right part or runs through all of it into the left's suffix.
narration.12: Double size until every value has its own leaf.
narration.15: Every node starts as EMPTY, so the padding leaves count as missing positions.
narration.17: Put each value of nums in its own leaf.
narration.19: Build the parents bottom-up, from the last internal node to the root.
narration.20: A node merges its two children, which cover the left and right halves of its range.
narration.24: Find the leaf that holds index.
narration.25: Replace that leaf with the new node.
narration.26: Walk up until the root has been rebuilt.
narration.28: Recombine the parent from its two children.
narration.37: Record index i under its value.
narration.40: With nothing removed, the root's best is the plain maximum subarray sum.
narration.41: Try removing each distinct value in turn.
narration.43: Blank out every occurrence of value.
narration.45: The root now describes the array without value; keep its best if it is larger.
narration.47: Put the occurrences back before trying the next value.
narration.50: The largest sum over all choices is the answer.
